done.why: I hit the 150-turn limit while heading back into the bank to try the vault again. I still had the lair chest and the bank vault unsolved, and I was out of open directions anyway. Several ways out ended in rockfalls that said whatever was beyond would have to wait.

about: It's the caverns south of a ravine where the exiled Wizard of Frobozz has retired with the Empire's stolen treasures. He keeps popping in to throw half-finished spells at you. You poke through a ruined underground estate: a formal garden with a unicorn, a dreary room with a crystal sphere, a looted bank and a dragon's lair. You get further by using your wits. Melting the ice with the dragon's own fire was the best example.

moments.note: The Wizard appears on the foot bridge, says 'Fantasize!' and vanishes cackling. A great entrance.
The 'grue' and the gold ingot were illusions. The room 'settles down and is only a room', and when I tried to take the ingot it was gone. A clever payoff for the spell.
Carousel south ends in a rockfall: 'Whatever lies beyond it will have to wait.' It's a dead end, but at least it's honest about it.
The place mat under the door and the letter opener in the keyhole worked first try. It's a satisfying old-school puzzle.
'pull place mat' gave two contradictory lines: 'You can't move the place mat' and then 'Moving the place mat reveals nothing.'
The dragon followed me once and then simply wasn't there in the next room. It took a couple of round trips to work out that I had to attack him in every room.
The dragon sees his reflection in the ice, breathes fire, melts the glacier and dies of the steam. That was the high point.
The passage the melting opened is blocked by another rockfall straight away. The reward was taken away.
The princess wakes in the lair and walks out. It's lovely that she moves on her own.
I lost track of the princess the moment I left the lair, and 'follow princess' didn't work.
The dead dragon is lying half across the Deep Ford. The world remembered what happened.
The unicorn bows to the princess, and she gives me a rose and the key and rides off side-saddle.
The gold key she 'handed' me wasn't in my inventory, and the unicorn was back with it still around its neck. Was that a Fantasize illusion or a bug? I couldn't tell.
'examine gold key' got the reply 'Unicorn? What unicorn?'
'You have the odd feeling that your pockets are your own again.' So the wizard's F-spell had done something to my things, but I never learned what.
I tried 'open chest' about six times and always got the same 'try again' message. It never opened.

wished: To keep the gold key the princess said she was handing me, or at least a clear sign of whether that scene was real
To follow the princess out of the lair
To actually get the rotten chest open, or a different message so I knew trying again was pointless
To go through the passage behind the melted glacier
To get some hint of how to get into the bank vault beyond walking through the curtain

lines.line: He peers at you from under his bushy eyebrows, as though you were not at all what he had been expecting, and had turned up anyway.
lines.why: It's funny, and it set the Wizard up as a petty, real presence.

lines.line: The room, which had been looking a little odd round the edges, settles down and is only a room.
lines.why: It quietly told me the grue and the ingot had been hallucinations.

lines.line: the public is advised not to let him finish a word.
lines.why: This was the newspaper's hint about the Wizard's spells. It gave me my goal: the treasures he took.

lines.line: There is a muffled explosion and the dragon, a puzzled expression on his face, dies.
lines.why: It was the payoff for luring him, and the funniest line I read.

lines.line: With that, she mounts the unicorn (side-saddle, of course) and rides off into the gloom.
lines.why: A charming end to the rescue.

lines.line: Whatever lies beyond it will have to wait.
lines.why: This line marked every dead end I hit, three times in all.

lines.line: You have the odd feeling that your pockets are your own again.
lines.why: A spell wearing off. It hinted that my inventory had been tampered with.

fun.why: The illusion trick, the door-key puzzle, the dragon and the princess with the unicorn were all fun to pull off. Repeating 'open chest' and the dragon round trips dragged a bit.

engagement.why: The newspaper gave me a goal, and each solved puzzle pulled me further in. My energy dropped at the chest and when the gold key went missing.

difficulty.why: The door and the dragon were fair once I'd thought them through. The chest and the bank vault beat me inside the turn limit, but the bank was fair. The chest felt more like a wall than a puzzle.

interestingness.why: The Wizard's spells, which make you doubt what you see, are a great idea, and the dead dragon left in the ford made the world feel alive. The gold key mix-up was intriguing but left me unsure whether something had gone wrong.

prose.why: It's witty, period-flavoured writing with good small touches, like the sphere that 'takes the red light and gives it back blue'. A few replies were clumsy: the double reply to 'pull place mat' on turn 37, and 'Unicorn? What unicorn?' on turn 115.
